issues.quote: The reflected wave from a rigid end can be written $y_r = -a\sin(kx+\omega t)$.
issues.problem: The notes do not state the incident wave. If the incident wave is the one used elsewhere, $y_i = a\sin(kx-\omega t)$, with the rigid end at x = 0, then $y_i + y_r = -2a\cos kx\sin\omega t$. This puts an antinode at the fixed end, which is impossible. It also contradicts the standing-wave form $y = 2a\sin kx\cos\omega t$ given in topics[10]. That form needs $y_r = +a\sin(kx+\omega t)$, which already includes the π phase change at a rigid boundary.
issues.correction: For an incident wave $y_i = a\sin(kx-\omega t)$ reflected at a rigid end at x = 0, the reflected wave is $y_r = a\sin(kx+\omega t)$, so that $y_i + y_r = 2a\sin kx\cos\omega t$ with a node at x = 0. State the incident wave explicitly, and note that NCERT writes $y_r = a\sin(kx+\omega t+\pi)$ only to illustrate the π phase change.
